claims.text: Adding rhenium and applying low-dose helium-ion implantation will increase yield strength relative to an alloy receiving neither intervention under high-temperature irradiation conditions.
The dual intervention will not negatively affect thermal stability.
The dual intervention will not negatively affect irradiation stability.
The proposed initial material is a magnetron-sputtered refractory high-entropy-alloy film without rhenium modification.
The proposed initial material has not undergone helium-ion implantation.
The intervention consists of rhenium alloying followed by controlled helium-ion implantation.
Testing above 800 °C with concurrent helium-ion irradiation reflects service environments relevant to high-temperature irradiation applications.
Rhenium will stabilize the alloy microstructure at elevated temperature.
Controlled helium-ion implantation will produce defect structures such as dislocation loops.
Helium-induced dislocation loops will act as pinning centers.
Rhenium addition will increase resistance to microstructural degradation at elevated temperature.
Helium-induced defects will retard dislocation motion under irradiation.
The effects of rhenium and helium-induced defects will act synergistically to improve mechanical performance.
The intervention can improve mechanical performance without causing deleterious phase changes.
The intervention can improve mechanical performance without causing embrittlement.
The beneficial effect will occur only within a limited rhenium-concentration window that avoids undesirable phase formation.
The beneficial effect will occur only within a helium-ion-dose window that creates useful defects without extensive microstructural damage.

contradictions.description: The baseline is defined as lacking helium-ion implantation, but the experiment says both the intervention and control sets are subjected to simulated irradiation using helium-ion beams. This may expose the nominal control to the same helium intervention and confound the comparison.

Helium implantation is described as a discrete treatment following rhenium alloying, while the conditions call for concurrent helium irradiation during high-temperature exposure and the experiment appears to include both an implantation step and a later helium-beam irradiation step. The intended irradiation sequence is therefore internally ambiguous.
